item.description:
🇨🇴 🚨 COLOMBIA: NATIONAL LEARNING SERVICE (SENA) ALLEGEDLY BREACHED, 20.5M CITIZEN RECORDS FOR SALE

A threat actor on a dark web forum claims to be selling a database of 20,564,434 unique records allegedly taken from SENA, Colombia's National Learning Service.

The actor claims the data includes:
• Full names and national ID numbers
• Dates of birth
• Addresses, phone numbers and emails
• Academic backgrounds and internship history
• Professional profiles and language skills
• Driver's license details

The data is said to come in JSONL and DB files, with a sample record shared to back the claim and payment requested in Bitcoin.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
If genuine, national IDs paired with contact details and career histories for more than 20 million people would fuel identity theft and convincing phishing that impersonates SENA or employers. SENA has not confirmed an incident. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.

#DDW #DarkWeb #Colombia #Government #DataLeak #ThreatIntelligence

item.description:
🇯🇵 🚨 PRESTIGE INTERNATIONAL BREACH EXPOSES UP TO 5.5M ROADSIDE-ASSISTANCE RECORDS

Tokyo-listed Prestige International says attackers took customer data from a business system its subsidiary Prestige Core Solution (PCS) uses to take and dispatch roadside-assistance requests for client companies.

• Up to ~5.5M records, a count that includes duplicates; the number of unique people is still being determined
• Data: names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, vehicle details (registration and chassis numbers), accident/breakdown request info and some bank-account details
• Intrusion detected Oct. 29; stolen credentials were disabled, but access continued and the system was shut down Oct. 30
• No credit card data leak confirmed; police and Japan's privacy regulator notified

⚠️ Analyst Note:
ENEOS separately says up to 8,500 of its car-lease contracts are affected; that is part of the same incident, not extra. Sony Assurance says its roadside desk is hard to reach and its customers' exposure is still being checked. No actor, ransomware claim or CVE has been disclosed. Expect phishing posing as insurers or roadside services.

item.description:
VIDEO | Delhi: In a conversation with PTI, Marina Romanello, Executive Director of The Lancet Countdown, discusses the issue of climate finance in its 10th annual report on Health and Climate Change, and how countries expected to provide such funding should respond when they themselves face climate-related challenges.

She says, “Every country is undoubtedly feeling the burden of climate change, and every country needs to step up its adaptation efforts. We see very few countries that have made sufficient progress. In fact, I don't think there is clear evidence that any country has adapted enough to climate change. Every country needs to intensify its efforts. However, it is important to note that no country will be safe from the health impacts of climate change until every country is safe. Therefore, when we pursue adaptation efforts, even in high-income countries with abundant resources, sharing that expertise and knowledge and supporting countries with fewer resources to catch up and avoid rapidly growing climate impacts in developing countries will benefit everyone.”

item.description:
VIDEO | Delhi: The Lancet Countdown Executive Director Marina Romanello speaks to PTI about its 10th annual report on Health and Climate Change and why progress in addressing climate-related health risks remains insufficient.

She says, “The latest reports from The Lancet Countdown show that the impacts of climate change are increasing and accelerating across multiple dimensions. This tells us that, despite ongoing efforts and some progress, adaptation has not kept pace with the rapidly warming planet and the increasingly severe impacts of climate change. This does not mean that adaptation has not taken place or that we have made no progress since the Paris Agreement entered into force. However, progress has fallen short. As a result, we are witnessing a growing global burden of disease associated with climate change... Today, around 30 per cent of countries report having Health National Adaptation Plans. However, we need to reach 100 per cent. Every country is affected by climate change, which means that 70 per cent of countries worldwide have not reported having a Health National Adaptation Plan.”

🇲🇽 🚨 MEXICO: DATABASE OF FEDERAL LABOR CONCILIATION REPRESENTATIVES ALLEGEDLY LEAKED

A threat actor group has leaked what they claim is a database of representatives registered on Mexico's labor conciliation platforms SINACOL and CENCOLAB. The data was shared on a dark web forum and a Telegram channel.

What the leak allegedly contains:
* Full names and contact details
* CURP national ID numbers
* RFC taxpayer registry numbers
* Details of legal powers of attorney and ID documents

⚠️ Analyst Note:
If authentic, CURP and RFC numbers paired with legal-representation records are a ready kit for identity fraud and for impersonating legal representatives in labor disputes. The number of affected people has not been stated, and the data may have been scraped from a portal rather than taken from back-end systems. No official confirmation that we are aware of. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.

A threat actor has posted what they claim is a database from Ponta, one of Japan's largest loyalty and reward point programs, operated by Loyalty Marketing, Inc. The post includes sample records with member details and full transaction ledgers.

What the leak allegedly contains:
* Ponta member IDs
* Full names, emails and phone numbers
* Postal codes and street addresses
* Transaction history with partner names, amounts and points balances

Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.

item.title: 🇸🇦 🚨 SAUDI ARABIA: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS LEAK OF 3.6GB OF MINISTRY OF DEFENSE DOCUMENTS A threat actor on a leak forum has published what they ...
item.description:
🇸🇦 🚨 SAUDI ARABIA: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS LEAK OF 3.6GB OF MINISTRY OF DEFENSE DOCUMENTS

A threat actor on a leak forum has published what they claim is a 3.6GB dump of secret documents from Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Defense. The files are being shared for download through third-party file-hosting and messaging links.

What the dump allegedly contains:
* Internal notices and circulars
* Records of private meetings
* Images of official documents
* Screenshots of WhatsApp conversations

⚠️ Analyst Note:
If authentic, internal military notices and staff chats could expose personnel, operations and internal processes, and would be useful for targeted phishing and espionage. Dumps like this often mix old, public or fabricated material with real files, and the WhatsApp images could come from a single compromised phone rather than ministry systems. The ministry has not confirmed an incident that we are aware of. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.

item.title: 🇺🇿 🚨 UZBEKISTAN PROBES REPORTED LEAK OF CITIZENS' ID AND VEHICLE DATA Uzbekistan's Interior Ministry says it has opened a joint review with t...
item.description:
🇺🇿 🚨 UZBEKISTAN PROBES REPORTED LEAK OF CITIZENS' ID AND VEHICLE DATA

Uzbekistan's Interior Ministry says it has opened a joint review with the State Security Service's Cybersecurity Center after databases said to hold citizens' personal data began circulating in Telegram bots on Oct. 28-29.

• Users report PINFL personal ID numbers, passport details, home addresses, phone numbers, vehicle plates, driving licence and vehicle registration data
• Posts link the records to SAFE Service (formerly SafeRoad, the traffic-fine app run with the ministry's traffic police), inDrive, Lada Auto, KiwiTaxi and Fargo
• SAFE Service denies any leak, saying the records were compiled from various sources before its app launched

⚠️ Analyst Note:
No breach has been confirmed. The origin of the data, the number of people affected and any link to the named services remain unverified. Aggregated "probiv" lookup bots often merge older leaks, so treat this as a combined-dataset exposure claim until the ministry reports its findings.

Research date: Oct 29-30, 2026 reports (reviewed Nov 3).

item.title: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has issued a clarification regarding the submission of Form 6 by previously enrolled voters whose names are mis...
item.description: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has issued a clarification regarding the submission of Form 6 by previously enrolled voters whose names are missing from the draft electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR). The ECI clarified that such voters must submit Form 6 to seek inclusion in the final electoral roll, irrespective of their previous enrolment, and that doing so does not amount to a false declaration. Citing the Delhi High Court's October 14, 2026, order in Nilotpal Datta & Anr. v. Election Commission of India & Ors., the Commission stated that no action under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, shall be initiated against an elector solely for submitting Form 6 during or after SIR, provided they are not already enrolled in another Parliamentary or Assembly Constituency and their declaration complies with the law. The ECI has also directed Chief Electoral Officers of all States and UTs to publicise the clarification widely in local languages through available media.
